- Quality: human-eval pass rate >= 90% on a 250-sample canonical intent holdout; safety filter false-positive rate < 3%

Thanks Susan — addressing your clarifying points and adding measurement detail we can operationalize.

1) Latency definition: The 95th percentile target I recommended is for end-to-end (request ingress at Redwood edge to last token emitted). If you need an on-prem / peered-only measurement we can add a second internal runtime-only KPI (95th runtime <= 200ms). Recommend we track both and surface both in the dashboard.

2) Quality plan: Yes — please send the stratified 150-session sample. Our human-eval protocol: double-blind scoring on canonical intents, scores bucketed (Accept / Minor Issue / Major Issue). Pass rate target is >=90% Accept; we treat Minor Issue as tolerable if downstream remediation <5%. We'll also run an automated semantic similarity check (embedding-based) for quick regression detection.

3) Security/ingest: For the initial evaluation we recommend VPC peering with a short-lived tunnel and an S3 bucket for payload exchange. If you prefer not to peer, we can set up secure signed uploads. Laura will own runbook steps for access provisioning.

Proposed acceptance matrix (short):
- Gate 1 (Week 1 smoke): median latency < 120ms; end-to-end errors < 0.5%
- Gate 2 (Week 3 throughput): sustain 40r/s for 1 hour with CPU/GPU utilization under threshold; cost telemetry enabled
- Gate 3 (Week 6 quality ramp): human-eval Accept >= 90% on 250 sample; safety filters pass
- Final (Week 8): overall pass on at least 3 of 4 primary signals (quality, latency, throughput, cost) with documented remediation plan for any misses.

I attached a short SLO proposal (slo-proposal.pdf) and pushed a measurement template to the drive link. On owners:
- Redwood runtime & instrumentation: Rishi (SE)
- Redwood onboarding & ops runbook: Laura (CS)
- Acme sampling & labelling: Susan / Rajiv

I’ll add measurement queries and dashboard links to the drive folder by Monday.
